purity_grades_silver.description: Sterling silver, most common for jewellery
Lower purity, used in some artefacts

huid_explanation: HUID stands for Hallmark Unique Identification. It is a 6-character alphanumeric code engraved on each piece of hallmarked jewellery, unique to that specific item. Consumers can verify a HUID using the BIS CARE app or the BIS Care website by entering the HUID number to confirm the jewellery's purity, hallmarking centre, and registration details.
how_to_verify: Look for the BIS hallmark logo (a triangle-like mark) on the jewellery
Check for the purity grade mark (e.g., 916 for 22K gold)
Check for the Assaying & Hallmarking Centre's identification mark
Enter the HUID on the BIS CARE app or BIS website to verify authenticity and details
jeweller_registration_note: As per BIS regulations, jewellers selling hallmarked jewellery must be registered with BIS. Consumers can check if a jeweller is BIS-registered via the BIS website's registered jeweller search.
